title: Accessible RTL transitions, locale-aware scrubber & number formatting prototype review
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Scope: Design and validate a prototype for the Cost Explorer timeline/scrubber and associated legends that satisfies WCAG 2.1 AA for keyboard users and screen readers, and is robust across locales (number/date formats) and RTL languages. The work focuses on three problem areas: 1) transition mirroring for RTL while preserving meaningful motion for reduced-motion users, 2) keyboard-first scrubber interactions (focus, range selection, announcement patterns) and 3) locale-aware numeric and time formatting in compact chart tooltips and legends (grouping separators, compact units, pluralization).

Goals: Ensure the scrubber and legend persistently read useful context to screen readers when moved, provide deterministic focus order for keyboard users (roving focus pattern), and render numbers/dates according to user locale while showing consistent units for cost/tokens. Provide a design solution that engineering can implement without custom per-locale logic beyond ICU formatting.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Keyboard: Left/Right arrow = move scrubber by step; Shift+Arrow = expand/shrink range; Home/End = jump to start/end; Space/Enter = toggle pinned tooltip. All interactions must expose a visible focus ring and announce changes via aria-live region with concise context (e.g., "Showing 3h–5h; cost: $1,234.56").
- Screen reader: Moving scrubber triggers short, non-repetitive announcements; the legend and active series label are programmatically associated with the scrubber position. For RTL locales announcements still read left-to-right logical ranges (start/end) while labels mirror visual order.
- i18n: Tooltip and legend numbers use ICU-style compact notation where appropriate, never truncate critical precision for billing contexts (min two decimal places for USD, configurable unit for tokens). Date ranges respect locale ordering (DD/MM/YYYY vs MM/DD/YYYY) and localized month names.
- Contrast & theme: Active scrubber handle and selected range meet 4.5:1 contrast on default theme and 3:1 on large text; a high-contrast token map is provided for theme overrides.
- Motion: Default transition uses eased opacity/translate; in reduced-motion contexts transitions are replaced with instant position changes and a 0.25s opacity fade to avoid focus loss.

Deliverables: Figma prototype with keyboard walkthrough, annotated spec for engineers (ARIA roles/attributes, example aria-live text, sample ICU number/date patterns), QA checklist for i18n team, and a short usability script for accessibility reviewers.
updates: 2025-03-12 - Kickoff: Aligned with PM about billing precision requirements; PM clarified two-decimal mandatory for USD lines and token units should allow compact but reveal exact on hover. Linked PM doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/pm-cost-formatting
2025-03-13 - Design: Created first Figma prototype focusing on RTL mirroring + keyboard focus flow. Prototype link: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/rtl-scrubber-prototype

2025-03-14 - Feedback from Eng (Marco Ruiz): Suggested shifting aria-live to polite and debounce announcements by 300ms to avoid spamming screen readers during continuous scrubbing. Added to spec as implementation note.

2025-03-15 - Accessibility review (Lina Chen): Noted that current focus ring uses token color with insufficient contrast in low-light theme. Proposed switching to elevated stroke token for focus and adding 2px fallback ring for high-contrast mode.

2025-03-16 - i18n sync (Sofia Nguyen): Confirmed ICU compact patterns for large numbers, requested examples for languages with narrow-number systems (hi-IN, zh-Hans). Added required examples to QA checklist.

2025-03-17 - Prototype update: Implemented shift+arrow range expand/shrink; added Home/End behavior; updated aria-live sample texts and debounce recommendation. Uploaded updated Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/rtl-scrubber-prototype?node-id=42
2025-03-18 - In Review: Sending to accessibility guild and i18n team for sign-off. Creating engineering spike for aria-live debounce and announcement semantics (ENG-24011).
notes: Trade-offs discussed: Avoid per-locale layout hacks; favor logical ordering + ICU formatting. This means some visual RTL mirroring will be purely presentational while screen reader order remains logical to reduce translator overhead.
Engineering constraints: Continuous scrubbing must not flood the event bus; recommend 60Hz sample with 300ms aria-live debounce and a single final announcement on mouseup/keyup.
Follow-ups: Create unit test matrix for i18n number formatting (en-US, en-GB, fr-FR, hi-IN, zh-Hans, ar-SA) and a small lab to validate screen reader output in VoiceOver and NVDA.
